newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean gov't to pay more for rice purchases.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean gov't to pay more for rice purchases.

text.p: The South Korean government plans to raise by three percent the price it will pay for this year's rice harvest, the Minstry of Agriculture and Forestry said on Wednesday.
The ministry said in a statement the purchase price for the 1997 crop would remain unchanged from 1996.
But the amount the government will purchase in 1996 would drop to 1.28 million tonnes, from 1.38 million in 1995.
The South Korean government buys rice from farmers after the harvest each year in order to stablise the supply and demand and prices of rice.
The statement said the government decided to raise the purchase price to support farmers.

It added that the government had no choice but to reduce the amount of the state's rice purchase. Under the World Trade Organisation's agreement, government subsidies fell by 75 billion won to 1.965 trillion won this year from 2.034 trillion won in 1995.
The goverment will spent 2.19 trillion won on the rice purchase programme this year, compared with 2.27 trillion in 1995. It will purchase 1.22 million tonnes of the 1997 crop.
This proposal must be approved by the National Assembly.

Earlier, South Korea said the country's rice output rose 13 percent to 5,323,000 tonnes this year from 4,695,000 tonnes in 1995, due to favourable weather and a sharp slowdown in the decline in the area of rice paddies.
